newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed up across the board on Wednesday due to a continued bull run on the A share markets, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 18.00 percent from 14.99 percent on Tuesday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell to 5.44 million lots from 8.88 million on Tuesday.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said the bull run on the Shanghai and Shenzhen A share markets boosted sentiment on the repo market.
In addition, six companies will issue or list A shares on the two exchanges on Thursday and Friday, so institutions are expected to borrow heavily on the repo market, they said.
"The repo rates are likely to continue to rise on Thursday due to all these favourable factors," said one trader.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed on Wednesday with liquidity continuing to flow out due the A share market bull run, traders said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, a market barometer, fell to 115.99 yuan from 116.04 yuan.
Combined volume of the seven-contract market fell to 0.99 million lots from 1.08 million lots.

The one-year bill that matures on April 2 this year stopped trading on Wednesday, reducing the number of contracts on the market to seven after the stoppage of the five-year note that matures on April 1 on Tuesday.
Traders said the spot contracts would have little potential for firm rises in the short term due to the bull run on the A share markets despite good mid-term prospects for the spot market.
